To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a programmable thermostat with multi-zoning is a better solution than a fixed setpoint thermostat for a single zone house.
a programmable thermostat can save energy by adjusting the heating schedule to fit the occupancy pattern, and the energy savings increase as the number of zones increase.

the programmable weekly schedule, based on the occupancy preference, and utility TOU rates, is the best option for energy conservation, and it can reduce the total energy consumption by 30% compared with the fixed set point schedule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simulator for a house heating system that can be used as an “expert shell” for future intelligent thermostat development.
the development of a simulator of a house energy consumption and associated cost, and its use as a tool for development of advanced intelligent control algorithms.
the development of a simulator of a programmable house heating system using an intelligent control algorithm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a controlled and programmably scheduled house heating system using a Programmable Communicative Thermostat (PST) and multi-zone house, would result in a significant savings in energy and energy cost.
a PCT with multi-zone controlled house, with a weekly programmable schedule, is the best choice for energy conservation.
a controlled house heating system, with programmable weekly schedule, and multi-zone control, is a more energy efficient and cost effective system, compared to a fixed schedule, single zone system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the simulation of house heating system using a C# programming language is a very useful tool in order to evaluate the efficiency of the system, energy consumption and the associated cost under various scenarios and conditions.

a PCT is an effective way to save money and energy by controlling the heating system, and that a multi-zone controlled house is an effective way of saving money and energy by reducing the total energy consumed by the house heating system.
a programmable schedule based on the occupant preferences and Utility Time-of-Use rates, can reduce the total energy cost by 20% or more, and can also reduce the total energy consumed by 15% or more.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the programmable schedule of PCTs can be used to optimize energy consumption, and hence energy costs, in the house heating system.
a PCT is a very useful tool for energy conservation and cost saving.
a programmable thermostat can reduce the energy costs by up to 30% compared to the fixed set points.
